data.title: FakeFs: match LocalFs on same-path move and copy into itself

data.body:
Fixes bug Bc07bf8feb4: ADP-fs ci timed out in the suite-lock queue three times (1800s, 3000s, 3400s; position #1-#6 of a queue with many agents) so the gate stays unavailable and the item cannot complete; a docs/adapter-only change that touches few files waits as long as a full-repo change Found on ADP-fs.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-Bc07bf8feb4 --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed Bc07bf8feb4 --regression-test <test>` first).

Not attached, they match nothing in the tree: ddflow/adapters/fs.py, ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py, tests/test_adapter_fs.py, tests/test_adapters_fs.py, tests/guard_baselines/importlinter-fs-home**, docs/ddflow/adapters/fs.md.

ROOT CAUSE (coordinator, 2026-11-04): _needs_suite_slot in ddflow/services/ci/runner.py counts selection plus always-run guard files against ci.selected_lock_tests. Always-run alone is 22 files, so all 436 recorded selected ci runs (min 24, median 78, max 178) took the one host-wide suite slot; PS-snapshot-calibrate ci queued 93 of 97 min. Operator raised the knob to 100 as a stopgap. SCOPE (operator 2026-11-04): stop counting always-run guards toward the limit, and base admission on measured run time or load rather than file count. Stay configurable, upgrade-safe, bounded; fall back to the file count when no durations are known. FALSIFIER: a small change's selected run still queues behind a full suite on an unloaded machine, or several large selections overlap and push load past the governor's limit.

Correction from the filer: the bug summary says all the ADP-fs ci timeouts were queue waits. Only the 1800 s run was observed blocked on the suite lock (its output showed queue positions #6 to #1). The 3000 s and 3400 s runs printed only 'timed out', so whether they were waiting or running the suite is unknown. A fourth run with --timeout 7200 was killed at the harness's 7200 s background limit with empty output and no recorded outcome. Part of the defect: `gate run` shows nothing on stdout while it waits, so a timed-out run cannot be told apart as lock wait or slow suite, and a gate timeout equal to the harness limit loses the outcome entirely.
